transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Location: Zoom - Internal
Recording: yes

Attendees: Maya C, Devon P, Samir R, Lina P, Owen B, Priya N, Claire M, Jordan L

--- Optional auto sections ---
Summary: (auto) Q1 planning, launch readiness, incident follow-ups
Topics: roadmap, launch checklist, incident review, canary plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay good morning everyone, thanks for being on time. I think we've got about an hour and 15. big agenda, roadmap slice and launch readiness for the hosted API improvements, and a short incident review about the token billing regression last week.
[00:20] Claire Morales: quick call out - we need decisions today on the canary length and the rollback criteria. exec is pushing for a tighter window but SRE will advise.
[00:35] Samir Rao: yeah so from SRE perspective, the regressions were spiky - the token billing mismatch appeared when prefix caching warmed up under heavy batching; it looks like a rounding bug in the billing aggregator. we've got a mitigation patch but want to validate in staging.
[00:50] Devon Patel: can you unpack that a little? was it quantization related, or batching logic?
[01:05] Samir Rao: it's not quantization, more in the batching path and prefix cache eviction interplay, so KV-cash - sorry KV cache - eviction + concurrency. some of the names in the logs were weird, "redwood dediacated" popped up, transcription of service names is messy in the traces, but the root cause seems to be a race when the aggregator combines token counts from cached responses with streaming increments.
[01:35] Lina Park: interesting. so failure mode was overcounting tokens then leading to incorrect billing spikes? which customers were affected?
[01:45] Samir Rao: small set of internal QA + two early customers on dedicated pools, low traffic but high batch sizes. we've got a repro and a fix, but we need to bake the patch in a canary with synthetic traffic that emulates real batching distribution.
[02:05] Owen Blake: for the canary, I'm proposing a staged ramp over 72 hours: 10% traffic for 24h, 30% for next 24h, then 60% for last 24h with automated anomaly checks on p95 latency and billing delta. rollback if billing delta > 1% or p95 increases by >25%.
[02:30] Claire Morales: 72 hours feels conservative but acceptable; exec wanted 48. what's the argument for 72?
[02:40] Owen Blake: last regression only surfaced after cache warmup and sustained batching for a few hours, so shorter windows might miss it. also we need time for incident commander handoffs across timezones.
[03:00] Jordan Lee: we also need to consider the canary on Dedicated vs Hosted - routing policies should keep Hosted stable; canary should target Dedicated first because the regression affected dedicated pools earlier.
[03:20] Maya Chen: OK noted - Priya, can you coordinate the canary schedule and make sure runbook is ready?
[03:28] Priya Nair: yep I'll publish the runbook and the checklist. I'll include the rollback steps and the telemetry dashboard links. I'll also set the slack alerting channel and the on-call rotation.
[03:40] Samir Rao: I'll prepare the staging benchmark — throughput, p95, and billing delta under synthetic batching. need folks to sign off on model variants to test.
[03:52] Maya Chen: what model variants? we said we wanted to validate both 8-bit quantized and float16, and a smaller 3B model to compare.
[04:05] Owen Blake: yes 3 configs: full fp16 large model, int8 quantized, and the 3B continuity model. we'll measure token cost, latency and memory. note: the quantized path had slightly different kernel selection so we want to be thorough.
[04:30] Devon Patel: on roadmap prioritization, we need to decide whether to include the model-ops automation tickets in the GA scope or push them to Q2. current velocity says pushing to Q2 keeps the launch low risk.
[04:45] Lina Park: tradeoff is that without model-ops automation we'll have manual steps during canary which increases operational load. what's the manual cost estimate?
[04:55] Owen Blake: about 2 FTE-days across the 72h canary for manual checks and rollbacks; if we include the automation, estimate is 3 weeks of dev time which would delay launch.
[05:15] Claire Morales: I'd rather accept the operational cost for GA and plan the automation in Q2. we can staff on-call and mitigate the risk.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: agree. commit to manual ops for GA but require hard SLOs and runbook, if the runbook is complete then proceed.
[05:35] Maya Chen: decision noted: de-prioritize model-ops automation to Q2, include into GA only manual runbook ops.
[05:45] Samir Rao: quick note on telemetry — we should add a billing delta monitor that compares aggregated tokens per route over rolling 60m windows and triggers if delta > 0.5% compared to baseline. that will give early warnings.
[06:05] Priya Nair: I'll add that to the checklist and share the grafana panels.
[06:15] Maya Chen: roadmap slice review — I'm going to show the prioritized list; high priority items are: 1) Hosted API streaming improvements, 2) Billing aggregator fix (must ship before GA), 3) Canary and rollback automation, 4) Observability dashboards for token-level cost. Medium priority: model-ops automation (moved to Q2), longer term: private deployment upgrade flow.
[06:45] Devon Patel: for the streaming improvements, do we have a perf estimate? Owen?
[06:52] Owen Blake: optimistic is 10-15% p95 reduction with improved batching and continuous kv cache reuse, but depends on kernel selector changes; we need the benchmark Samir mentioned to confirm.
[07:10] Claire Morales: okay, is there any blocker that would definitely postpone GA?
[07:18] Samir Rao: the blocker would be if the staging benchmarks show >20% p95 regression or if the billing delta can't be stabilized under synthetic load. both are guardrails.
[07:35] Maya Chen: refer back to timeline — we have a target GA date in mid-January; that gives us six weeks. action owners, please follow the due dates.
[07:50] Lina Park: on customer comms, we'll prepare a heads-up and a post-launch status update template. include the known risk about canary and invite customers to opt into early access.
[08:05] Owen Blake: note — competitor moves: Anthropic launched some inference optimizations. not a blocker but some customers will ask about perf comparatives. have a short benchmark doc ready.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: also check legal for any change in billing terms if the billing aggregator changes how token accounting looks to customers. procurement/legal touchpoint.
[08:35] Maya Chen: good flag — Lina please loop in Legal for the messaging and check if we need updated billing statements.
[08:45] Lina Park: will do.
[08:50] Maya Chen: ok last section - incident review specifics: Samir, walk us through the repro and the patch status.
[09:00] Samir Rao: repro is in internal repo - I'll link it. patch is in review and fixes the race in the aggregator merge path; we added a durable delta reconcile step. quick caveat: it increases latency by ~0.5-1% in synthetic tests, but we're measuring cost vs correctness.
[09:30] Devon Patel: can we optimize the reconcile step later? maybe async reconcile with eventual correction?
[09:40] Samir Rao: yep that is plan B — for GA we'll take the safer approach and keep reconcile synchronous, later we can move to eventual consistency with customer-facing account adjustments.
[09:58] Priya Nair: I'll add the patch rollforward steps into the runbook and note any caution.
[10:05] Maya Chen: perfect. final recap, decisions: 72-hour canary targeted at Dedicated pools first, manual model-ops for GA, must pass staging benchmark, billing aggregator patch required pre-GA, runbook and telemetry must be published.
[10:25] Claire Morales: thanks everyone. I'll expect the checklist from Priya by Friday.
[10:35] Maya Chen: thanks, I'll publish roadmap slice and send calendar invites for canary prep sessions. Meeting adjourned.

End of recording.
